subject: Clarification on breach handover obligations, subprocessor notifications, and evidence transfer
messages:
From: Elena Mendez <elena.mendez@dataguard.io>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Clarify breach handover timelines and subprocessor obligations

Jonas — thanks for the walkthrough yesterday. A couple of quick clarifying asks from our security and legal teams so we can sign off on the DPA redlines: 

1) Notification window — your DPA says "prompt" notification. For our regulators we need a firm initial alert timeline (e.g., 24h from detection to customer notification). Can Redwood commit to an initial notification SLA and what triggers that (detection vs confirmed exfiltration)?

2) Evidence export scope & timing — when a customer requests forensic artifacts, what is the expected delivery cadence? We typically expect preliminary artifacts (logs, hashes, metadata) within 72 hours, then a full export within a defined window. Can you outline what Redwood can deliver and any constraints (esp. when subprocessors are involved)?

3) Subprocessor involvement — if a subprocessor actually holds the affected data (or controls telemetry), does Redwood undertake to notify and coordinate with that subprocessor on the customer's behalf? What timelines and proof of cooperation can you provide?

4) Transfer mechanism & custody — we need to know whether Redwood will provide a secure handoff (SFTP + checksum) vs an escrow arrangement (time-limited HSM access). Also, will chain-of-custody docs be provided?

If you can share a brief proposed clause we can circulate internally. Attached are the redlines we proposed earlier (we referenced your managed export flows).

Appreciate a short reply we can share with Legal/Security.

— Elena
Elena Mendez
Head of Security Operations, Dataguard Inc.
attachment: dataguard_dpa_redlines_20261108.pdf (pdf)

From: jonas_weber@redwood.com
To: Elena Mendez <elena.mendez@dataguard.io>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 11:45:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Clarify breach handover timelines and subprocessor obligations

Elena — thanks for the concrete list. Below is a concise summary of Redwood's operational posture and a proposed clause (I'll attach a doc with clean text). High level: we try to balance regulator expectations with operational and subprocessor constraints.

1) Notification window: Redwood's standard is an initial triage notification to affected customers within 24 hours of detection where detection is defined as "confirmed unauthorized access or exfiltration that materially affects customer data." We will add a definitional sentence in the clause to avoid ambiguity.

2) Evidence export cadence: We can commit to providing preliminary forensic artifacts (transactional logs, redacted stacks, and metadata + hash manifests) within 72 hours of an agreed evidence request. Full dataset exports (if applicable) typically require coordination with any relevant subprocessors and a legal request; target window for staged delivery is 10 business days from request acceptance for large exports. Constraints: if a subprocessor is in a jurisdiction with export restrictions, we will either provide attestations and aggregated artifacts or facilitate a direct, auditable handoff via the subprocessor.

3) Subprocessor coordination: Redwood will notify subprocessors in scope within 48 hours when their services are implicated. We will use our subprocessor liaison process to obtain artifacts; however, we cannot unilaterally compel third-party subprocessors to export data faster than their regional controls permit. The clause can include a cooperation commitment and a fallback (attestation + escrow access).

4) Transfer & custody: Preferred transfer is SFTP over a vetted, ephemeral bucket with checksums and hash manifests. For higher assurance customers we offer an escrow path: time-limited HSM-wrapped exports via a certified third-party escrow vendor. Chain-of-custody manifests will accompany exports; signatures/PKI assertions can be generated on request.

Next steps: attached is a proposed clause with staged timelines and fallback language. If that's acceptable, we can add the clause as an exhibit to the DPA and include a short ops-impact appendix so you know when special approvals are required.

If you want a quicker phone call to walk legal through the wording, happy to set 30 minutes.

— Jonas Weber
Director, Legal & Privacy (Redwood Inference)
attachment: redwood_proposed_breach_clause_20261111.docx (docx)

From: kimberly_park@redwood.com
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 11:55:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Clarify breach handover timelines and subprocessor obligations

Jonas — quick operational notes / flags from Legal & Ops: 

- 24h initial notification is doable as a "best effort" for detection-confirmed incidents, but we should avoid an unconditional contractual SLA without an exceptions clause (e.g., ongoing investigation where disclosure would impede remediation or regulatory freeze). Propose language: "Redwood will use commercially reasonable efforts to notify within 24 hours, except where notification could materially impede remediation or where legal restrictions apply."

- 72h preliminary artifacts OK for small/medium incidents; for high-volume telemetry sets this may be infeasible without sampling. Ops asks that we include a delivery profile (small/medium/large) with expected timelines in an appendix. See attached ops impact note.

- Subprocessor EU-hosted telemetry: requires an extra approval thread and sometimes 3-7 business days to process. We should call that out as a potential delay and offer an alternative attestation + escrow access option.

I'll sync with Ben on the fallback attestation wording.

— Kimberly Park
Head of Privacy Operations, Redwood Inference
attachment: ops-impact-note.pdf (pdf)

From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 13:10:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Clarify breach handover timelines and subprocessor obligations

Agree with Kimberly. Suggested compromise clause structure (summary):

- Initial alert: within 24 hours of detection (subject to exceptions where notification would impede remediation or legal prohibition).
- Preliminary artifacts: within 72 hours, limited to logs, metadata, and hash manifests.
- Full dataset: delivered in staged buckets; target 10 business days for the majority of exports, subject to subprocessor permissions and export controls.
- Fallback: if Redwood or a subprocessor cannot export data due to legal/regulatory constraints, Redwood will deliver a signed attestation describing the scope of data accessed, provide query-level extracts where possible, and provide escrowed access to a neutral third party for independent verification.

Inline suggested text (for insertion into the DPA):
"Upon Customer request following a Security Event, Redwood will (a) notify Customer pursuant to the Notification provisions, (b) provide preliminary forensic artifacts (logs, metadata, and hash manifests) within seventy-two (72) hours of an accepted request, and (c) initiate a staged export process for full datasets with a target delivery window of ten (10) business days, subject to subprocessor consents, export controls, and reasonable operational limitations. In cases where export of Customer Data is prevented by third-party subprocessor controls or applicable law, Redwood will provide a written attestation of impacts and facilitate access via an independent escrow provider where feasible."

I can draft the exhibit with delivery profiles.

— Ben Carter
VP, Security Partnerships, Redwood Inference

From: jonas_weber@redwood.com
To: Elena Mendez <elena.mendez@dataguard.io>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 16:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Clarify breach handover timelines and subprocessor obligations

Elena — thanks, team. Below is the wording Redwood proposes for the DPA exhibit. It's intended to be clear, operationally realistic, and includes the fallback attestation/escrow path to address subprocessor/export constraints. Please let me know if Dataguard can accept this or wants tighter timelines on any element. We can call Legal tomorrow to finalize.

Proposed Exhibit: Incident Assistance and Evidence Handover

1. Definitions: For purposes of this Exhibit, "Detection" means Redwood's determination, based on its internal telemetry and triage processes, of unauthorized access or exfiltration of Customer Data. "Accepted Request" means a Customer-requested evidence export acknowledged by Redwood within 24 hours of receipt.

2. Notification: Redwood will use commercially reasonable efforts to notify the Customer of a Detection within twenty-four (24) hours of such Detection, provided that such notification does not materially impede remediation efforts or is otherwise legally prohibited.

3. Preliminary Artifacts: Upon an Accepted Request, Redwood will provide preliminary forensic artifacts (including, where available, operational logs, metadata, and hash manifests) within seventy-two (72) hours. These artifacts will be scoped to impacted systems and redacted for third-party PII where required.

4. Staged Exports: Redwood will initiate a staged export of full Customer Data where applicable, with a target of ten (10) business days for completion of the first full export batch. Timing is subject to subprocessors' cooperation, applicable export controls, and reasonable operational limitations. Redwood will provide a delivery profile (Small/Medium/Large) as an appendix to set expectations for large telemetry sets.

5. Subprocessor Coordination and Fallback: Where third-party subprocessors control or host affected data and cannot export due to legal or contractual restrictions, Redwood will: (a) notify the Customer of the constraint; (b) provide a signed attestation describing the scope of the impact and the data types inaccessible; and (c) where feasible, facilitate independent escrow access to the relevant data through a mutually agreed third-party escrow provider.

6. Transfer Mechanism and Custody: Data transfers will be performed over secure, ephemeral channels (SFTP or pre-signed, time-limited object storage) with accompanying checksum manifests and chain-of-custody documents. Where additional assurance is required, Redwood will use vendor HSM-wrapped exports and PKI-signed attestations.

7. Exceptions and Escalation: Any deviation from these timelines will be communicated to the Customer, with an explanation and expected completion estimate. Critical or high-impact incidents may be escalated to executive liaison teams to agree on deviations.

If Dataguard agrees to this structure, we'll attach the exhibit and the delivery-profile appendix. Attached is the doc with the same text for easy redlining. Happy to hop on a call tomorrow at 9:30am PT if that helps move this over the line.

— Jonas Weber
Director, Legal & Privacy (Redwood Inference)
